items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: One of the first young French jazz musicians that I made acquaintance with was a tenor player named Alex Combelle.

ctx.x: But at the Villa d'Este, we played matinees which were called teen-dances every day from 5 until 7 in the afternoons and 9.30 until 2 the next morning and had no nights off. My first visit in Paris had been so short that the city was still new and exciting at this time and the routine of playing two hours every day and four hours and a half every night was like a happy game.

One of the first young French jazz musicians that I made acquaintance with was a tenor player named Alex Combelle. Exactly how we met, I cannot recall, but I remember that Alex Combelle used to come to my room in the Hotel Eden and ask me about many musicians in the States and especially about ones around New York. Alex spoke English quite well. All that I knew to say in French was : 'bonjour, monsoir' and 'oui' (wee).

I had a photograph album with some photos of different musicians I had worked with and showed them to Alex. He knew about quite a few of them and besides Armstrong, he had heard about Henri "Red" Allen but never seen a photo of him. He pointed to Red's photo and asked me who he was. I told him it was Red Allen. His comment was: Hum, funny face!
